title.narrative: Strengthened capacities of tripartite constituents to facilitate the transition of economic units in the informal economy to formality

description.narrative: Namibia’s labour markets and economy are characterized by increasing prevalence of informality, with a significant proportion of workers and enterprises operating outside formal regulatory and social protection systems, particularly in sectors such as agriculture, retail trade and informal services. Informal employment disproportionately affects women, youth and rural populations, and is often associated with low productivity, precarious working conditions, limited access to finance and markets, and weak coverage of labour rights and social protection. Despite its role as a critical source of employment and livelihoods, the informal economy remains insufficiently integrated into national development strategies, underscoring the need for coherent and evidence-based formalization pathways. The ILO has supported Namibia in advancing a diagnosis of informality in 2025, generating evidence on its scale, characteristics and drivers. A policy framework articulating formalization priorities has been outlined, aligned to broader UN efforts under the Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transitions, which promotes integrated approaches combining employment coordination and creation; and extension of social protection coverage. The ILO is supporting the Government of Namibia and social partners to strengthen policies and programmes that facilitate a gradual and inclusive transition from the informal to the formal economy. The intervention focuses on improving understanding of informality, strengthening labour protection, simplified registration systems, incentives for formalization, access to financial and business development services, skills upgrading, and extension of labour rights and social protection to informal workers. The ILO also promotes integrated, area-based and sector-specific approaches, particularly in high-informality sectors, linking formalization to value chain development and job creation initiatives, especially for youth and women.
